turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Meena, come, sit. You look a bit washed out. What's been going on?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, actually I am tired only. I do one small thing and I want to lie down. And the periods have become too much, that is the main thing, or maybe the tiredness is, I don't know where to start.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Start wherever you like. The periods, or the tiredness.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Periods, then. It's been about a year, since Diwali or after Diwali, I can't place it properly. Heavy, with clots. My sister came in with me, she forced me to come.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I stay with her, doctor. She is not managing. Even one flight of stairs and she is breathing like she ran.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): So breathless on the stairs as well. Meena, how long has all this been building?

[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): The tiredness, last winter, or the one before, I really cannot say. Don't ask me the month. The breathing is more these past few months, if I walk fast or take the stairs. On the flat I am okay.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): And with the periods, how many pads are you using?

[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Some days six, some days eight or nine, I lose count, what to say. Not every day the same. Clots, big ones, like a coin, sometimes bigger, I didn't measure. It goes on six days, seven days, before it was four and finished.

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Hair also, a full comb of it in the morning. My daughter is in tenth, board year, she saw the bathroom drain and made a face. And her auto was late yesterday, the whole house was shouting, I hadn't even had tea. Sorry, that is not your problem.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): It's alright, you're tired and the house is busy. Any fever with this, or pain low down with the bleeding?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Fever, no. Pain is the usual period pain only, not something new. I take a hot water bag and I manage.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): When the breathing comes, is there chest pain?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose... sometimes, not really. Not a pain I can point to. More like I am finished, that's all.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Okay. I won't write that down as chest pain. Any giddiness, or a feeling you might faint?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Giddy, yes, if I get up quick from the bed. I sit on the edge and it goes. Fainting, no, I haven't fallen.
[SEG0017] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Last month in the kitchen she went very pale. She didn't fall, I caught her arm. She will say it was nothing.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): A near-faint once, noted. Are you taking any tablets?

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Iron, sometimes. They said my haemoglobin is low, so the chemist gave ferrous sulphate, one a day. I take it two times or three times in a week, when I remember, not daily.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you know how many milligrams?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): I think 200 mg. I'm not fully sure, I didn't see the strip today. Maybe it is 200.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any other tablets, thyroid or blood pressure?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing else. Last clinic they said BP is normal. I don't have a machine at home. My neighbour checks hers every morning, she is very particular, I am not like that.
[SEG0024] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Doctor, since you asked about thyroid, our mother had thyroid. She was on tablets for years. Mother's sister also, the same thing.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thank you, that helps. Any allergy, to a medicine or a food?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that. I eat everything, even the neighbour's very spicy biryani, no problem. That was last Sunday, different topic.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): The iron, you skip it. Does it upset your stomach?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Constipation, yes, the stomach becomes hard, so I skip. And I forget. Morning is tiffin, then the school auto, and if I remember at night I think, leave it.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): If you do take it, is it with tea?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): With the morning tea, when I take it. Everybody in my house takes tablets with tea, I thought it is the same.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tea holds the iron back a little. Plain water is better, and a bit of lemon or orange if you have it. We'll sort the plan in a minute.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Bleeding from the nose, blood in the stool, or bruises coming easily?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Only the periods. Stool is normal colour, and the nose never bleeds.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Urine, any burning or going more often?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Burning, no. I wake once in the night to pass urine when the bleeding is on, not otherwise. Daytime is normal.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sleep itself, and weight, any change?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Sleep is okay, I am tired so I sleep. Weight, I think the salwar is loose, but I didn't weigh. My sister will say a number, she always does.
[SEG0038] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I would guess two or three kilos, over some months. We don't have a scale, so don't take my word.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Then we won't put a number. Let me examine you. Pulse is 98, blood pressure is 108 over 72, and the palms and the inside of the eyes are pale.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Lungs are clear, the ankles are not swollen, and the heart sounds are normal, just a bit quick.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): 98, is that bad? My cousin was 120 and they kept her, but that was after delivery, totally different, I shouldn't compare.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): A bit fast for sitting still, it fits with low blood, not an emergency like your cousin. I'm not worried about the heart from what I hear.

[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): My working thought is low iron from the heavy periods, possibly anaemia. I can't confirm it till the blood tests. Tiredness and hair loss could also be thyroid, with your mother's history, so that stays as a possibility, not a diagnosis.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): So not cancer? I keep thinking of my friend's sister, she had bleeding and it was something serious, and I didn't sleep one night.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): From what you've told me I am not suspecting cancer. We look for iron and thyroid first, those are the likely things.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): Today I'll send a full blood count, a ferritin, and a TSH. A pelvic scan we might do if the bleeding is still this heavy once we see the bloods. Not booking it today.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): The scan is the jelly one on the stomach? I had that when I was pregnant, years ago, the baby was fine, that is old news.

[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Same sort of scan, only if we still need it. For the iron, please take ferrous sulphate 200 mg once a day, by mouth, every day, for the low iron. Not just two or three times a week.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Every day, even with the hard stomach?

[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): Try every day. If the constipation is too much, tell me and we can adjust. Not with tea. Some greens, a little jaggery, lemon in the dal, that supports you, but the tablet is the main part.
[SEG0051] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll put the strip near the dining table. In the cupboard she will never see it.
[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): That will help. Come back in two weeks with the reports. Sooner if a pad is soaking through every hour, or if you feel you will faint again.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks, okay. The blood test, should I come fasting? I didn't eat much this morning anyway, only half a dosa, the rest I gave my daughter.
[SEG0054] person_1 (DOCTOR): No fasting for these. They can take the blood today before you leave.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright. And doctor, the clots, I said coin size, sometimes it feels bigger, I am not measuring with a scale, you understand.
[SEG0056] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She changes the bedsheet some nights. That part she didn't say.
[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): Heavy enough, I've got the picture, we don't need an exact clot size. We'll talk again when the reports are in.
